text:
ConocoPhillips rose 1.6% today, snapping a three-day losing streak and bouncing back from a two-week decline of 7.6%. The move likely reflects cautious optimism around oil prices after a report that the Trump administration believes the Iran conflict could end "fairly soon"—any reduction in Middle Eastern tensions typically supports crude prices, and investors may be rotating back into energy stocks after selling them down last week. Brent crude did dip below $90 briefly on those peace hopes, but U.S. crude is still holding near $100 a barrel, and the company's recent quarterly earnings report may also be stabilizing sentiment.

The bigger picture here is that oil majors like ConocoPhillips have been under pressure lately, down 7.6% in two weeks, likely as markets priced in lower crude prices if geopolitical risks ease—but today's rebound suggests investors see a floor and aren't convinced a lasting peace deal is imminent, so the energy sector isn't capitulating yet.
